netNewFindings.title: Orders page pagination uses useState instead of useUrlState, inconsistent with status filter
netNewFindings.description: The orders page syncs the status filter with URL via useUrlState (line 66) but uses local useState for currentPage (line 68). This means pagination state is lost on back/forward navigation while status filter is preserved, creating an inconsistent and confusing UX. Products page uses useUrlState for all state. This is different from R5.SUP.008 which covered a different page's pagination — this finding is specific to the status filter/pagination split inconsistency on the same page.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.008 covers 'Pagination state not URL-synced'. However, the NEW aspect here is the inconsistency within the same page: statusFilter uses useUrlState but currentPage does not. R5.SUP.008 was a general finding, not about intra-page inconsistency. Borderline but the split-brain aspect is net new.
netNewFindings.impact: User selects status 'shipped' on page 3, clicks an order, presses back — they return to 'shipped' filter but page 1 instead of page 3.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Replace `const [currentPage, setCurrentPage] = useState(1)` with `const [currentPageStr, setCurrentPageStr] = useUrlState('page', '1'); const currentPage = parseInt(currentPageStr, 10) || 1;`

netNewFindings.title: BNPL orders hardcodes limit=100 with no pagination, silently truncates data for high-volume suppliers
netNewFindings.description: The fetchBnplOrders function hardcodes `params.set('limit', '100')` (line 42) and the page renders all results without any pagination controls. For suppliers with more than 100 BNPL-backed orders, the user never sees orders beyond the first 100 and has no way to discover this. Unlike other list pages (products, orders, invoices) which have pagination, BNPL orders silently truncates. There is no 'showing X of Y' indicator either.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers this. R5.SUP.008 covers pagination URL sync. R5.SUP.030 covers mobile responsive view. This is about missing pagination entirely.
netNewFindings.impact: Supplier with 150+ BNPL orders never sees the oldest 50+, potentially missing overdue payments or important financial data.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add pagination state and controls matching the pattern used in orders/invoices pages. Show total count from backend response.

netNewFindings.title: Notifications page uses manual fetch pattern instead of TanStack Query, missing retry/cache/dedup
netNewFindings.description: Every other data-fetching page in the supplier portal (dashboard, products, orders, invoices, earnings, BNPL, chat, KYC) uses TanStack React Query for data fetching. The notifications page (line 9 imports only useState/useEffect/useCallback) manually implements its own fetch-loading-error pattern (lines 32-46). This means notifications lack: automatic retry on network failure, query caching/deduplication, stale-while-revalidate, and background refetch. This is an architectural inconsistency that reduces resilience.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers this. R5.SUP.026 covers color palette inconsistency. This is about data-fetching pattern inconsistency.
netNewFindings.impact: Notifications are the only page without automatic retry — a transient network blip shows a permanent error state until manual refresh. Other pages recover silently.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Refactor to use useQuery from @tanstack/react-query with the same pattern as other pages: `const { data, isLoading, isError, refetch } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['notifications', offset], queryFn: fetchFn })`

netNewFindings.title: markAsRead and markAllAsRead silently swallow errors with no user feedback
netNewFindings.description: Both markAsRead (lines 50-57) and markAllAsRead (lines 59-66) catch errors with empty catch blocks (`catch { // Silently handle }`). While the UI optimistically updates the isRead state, if the server rejects the request (e.g., due to auth expiry), the user sees the notification as read but it will revert on page refresh. Unlike other pages where mutations use toast.error for failure feedback, these operations give zero indication of failure.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers silent error swallowing in notification operations. This is net new.
netNewFindings.impact: User marks notification as read, but server rejects (401 or 500). Notification appears read until next page load when it reappears as unread, causing confusion.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add toast.error in catch blocks: `catch (err) { toast.error('Failed to mark as read'); }`. Optionally revert the optimistic UI update on failure.

netNewFindings.title: Chat conversations hardcode limit=100 with no pagination, silently drops older conversations
netNewFindings.description: The chat page fetches conversations with `?limit=100` (line 69) and messages with `?limit=100` (line 83), but never provides pagination or infinite scroll. Suppliers with more than 100 conversations will never see older ones. Similarly, conversations with more than 100 messages will show only the 100 most recent with no way to scroll back further. The BNPL page has the same problem (DA6-SUP-002) but chat is more critical since message history has legal/business significance.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.011 covers inline styles and mobile responsiveness of chat. This finding is about data truncation, which is a different concern entirely. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Long-running supplier-retailer conversations lose message history beyond 100 messages. Order dispute resolution context could be lost.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add infinite scroll or 'Load more' button for both conversation list and message thread. Track total count from API response.

netNewFindings.title: Chat mark-as-read fires on every conversation selection regardless of current read status
netNewFindings.description: When a conversation is selected (line 95-98), the mark-as-read API call fires unconditionally via `chatApiFetch(...read, { method: 'PATCH' })`. Even if all messages in the conversation are already read, this PATCH fires on every click. This creates unnecessary API load and potential race conditions if the user clicks between conversations quickly.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers this. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Each conversation click generates a PATCH request even when unnecessary. With 10s refetch interval on conversations, this could also cause stale data if mark-read and conversation list fetch overlap.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Guard the call: `if (selectedConvId && conversations.find(c => c.id === selectedConvId)?.unreadCount > 0)`

netNewFindings.title: Register page (1495 lines) is a single monolithic 'use client' component with no code splitting
netNewFindings.description: The register page is 1495 lines in a single file with 'use client' directive. It includes all 5 registration steps (phone, OTP, details, documents, success), document upload logic with XHR, camera capture, and state persistence. This entire bundle loads upfront even though a user only interacts with one step at a time. No React.lazy or dynamic imports are used. Similarly, orders page is 1025 lines. This causes unnecessarily large client-side JS bundles.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: LIVE.SUPPLIER.SSR_REGISTER_DEGRADED.001 covers SSR degradation for register page. This finding is about bundle size and code splitting, not SSR support. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Register page loads ~1495 lines of JS for all steps when user only needs step 1. On slow 3G connections common in Indian mobile users (the target demographic), this adds 2-3s to initial load.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Split each step into a separate component and use Next.js dynamic imports: `const DocumentStep = dynamic(() => import('./DocumentStep'))`. XHR upload logic should be lazy-loaded.

netNewFindings.title: Orders badge mark-read pathname comparison will fail under basePath /supplier
netNewFindings.description: Line 79 compares `pathname === '/orders'` to trigger markOrdersRead. However, with Next.js basePath: '/supplier' configured in next.config.js (line 61), the usePathname() hook returns the path WITHOUT the basePath prefix. So pathname will be '/orders' and the comparison works. BUT this is fragile — if the route is ever nested (e.g., '/orders/123'), the strict equality fails and mark-read never fires. The existing R5.SUP.004 finding covered a different concern about basePath itself, but the actual code still uses strict equality instead of startsWith.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.004 covers 'Orders read-marking compares bare pathname without basePath'. That finding was about basePath stripping. This is about the strict equality vs startsWith problem — if a user deep-links to /orders/123 and navigates back to /orders, the badge may not clear because the initial pathname was not '/orders'. Borderline overlap but the root cause (strict equality) persists. PARTIALLY_OVERLAPS with R5.SUP.004.
netNewFindings.impact: Edge case: deep-linking to a specific order URL then navigating to orders list may not clear the badge.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Change to `pathname.startsWith('/orders')` to match both /orders and /orders/[id].

netNewFindings.title: Error boundary 'Go Home' navigates to / which redirects to /supplier, ignoring auth state
netNewFindings.description: The root error boundary (error.tsx line 20) and global-error.tsx (line 65) both use `window.location.href = '/'` for the 'Go Home' action. With basePath: '/supplier', the next.config.js redirect sends / to /supplier. But the root page.tsx then checks auth: if authenticated, redirect to /dashboard; if not, to /login. This creates an unnecessary redirect chain: / -> /supplier -> /dashboard or /login. The error boundary should navigate directly to the appropriate destination.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.027 covers '404 page always links to dashboard even for unauthenticated users'. This finding is about error boundaries (not 404) and the redirect chain, not the auth-state-unaware destination. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: After an error, user experiences 2-3 redirects before reaching the right page, adding latency and potential for additional errors during recovery.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Use `window.location.href = '/supplier/dashboard'` or better, check auth cookie first: `window.location.href = document.cookie.includes('sm_auth=') ? '/supplier/dashboard' : '/supplier/login'`

netNewFindings.title: Global error boundary renders bare html/body without font, theme, or CSS, creating jarring visual break
netNewFindings.description: The global-error.tsx renders its own <html><body> with only inline styles (lines 15-83). It has no Inter font (the font used by root layout), no Tailwind CSS classes, no dark mode support, and no theme consistency. When this error boundary triggers, the user sees a completely different visual design from the rest of the portal. This is technically correct for Next.js (global-error replaces root layout) but the visual discontinuity is poor UX.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers global error boundary styling. R5.SUP.032 covers EmptyState/DashboardError dark mode, not global-error.tsx. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: If root layout crashes, the error page looks like a completely different website — no branding, no font, different colors — which may confuse users or reduce trust.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add minimal inline CSS that approximates the Inter font via system-ui fallback and matches the portal's color scheme. Consider embedding a minimal <style> tag with the critical styles.

netNewFindings.title: Invoice PDF download uses relative URL but omits API_BASE_URL, inconsistent with other file operations
netNewFindings.description: The downloadPdf function (line 51) fetches from `/api/v1/supplier/invoices/${invoiceId}/pdf` using a relative URL. While this works through the nginx reverse proxy in production, it is inconsistent with the pattern used in api.ts where all endpoints use `${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/...`. The KYC upload, CSV upload, and image upload all use API_BASE_URL. If API_BASE_URL is set to a non-empty value (e.g., for local development against a remote backend), PDF downloads will fail while other API calls succeed.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.001 covers 'Invoice PDF download uses relative URL without API_BASE_URL causing 404 in production'. The title says 'done' but examining the actual code, the fix appears to have been marking the finding as done while the code still uses a relative URL at line 51. If the fix was to make relative URLs work via nginx, then this is no longer a P0 but the inconsistency with other upload endpoints remains. PARTIALLY_OVERLAPS with R5.SUP.001.
netNewFindings.impact: In development environments where API_BASE_URL points to a remote backend, PDF downloads silently fail while all other API calls work.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Import API_BASE_URL from api.ts and use `${API_BASE_URL}/api/v1/supplier/invoices/${invoiceId}/pdf`.

netNewFindings.title: Register layout renders its own Toaster instance, creating duplicate toasts with root Providers
netNewFindings.description: The register layout (line 43-56) renders its own `<Toaster>` component. The root layout.tsx wraps all pages in `<Providers>` which includes its own `<Toaster>` (Providers.tsx lines 27-51). Since register is a child of root layout, both Toasters are active simultaneously. This means toast.success/error calls will render TWO toast notifications — one from Providers and one from the register layout Toaster.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.021 covers 'Duplicate Toaster rendered in both Providers and layout components'. This finding identifies the SPECIFIC instance in register/layout.tsx that was not fixed. The register layout still has its own Toaster at line 43. OVERLAPS with R5.SUP.021 — this is the same bug in the specific file that was presumably supposed to be fixed. Marking as RESIDUAL.
netNewFindings.impact: Every toast during registration appears twice — once from Providers, once from register layout.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Remove the `<Toaster>` from register/layout.tsx since it is already provided by root Providers.

netNewFindings.title: KYC page bank verification and Profile page bank details update the same data through different APIs
netNewFindings.description: The KYC page has a Bank Verification tab that calls `verifyBankAccount()` (api.ts line 853) which hits `/api/v1/supplier/kyc/verify-bank`. The Profile page Bank Details tab calls `updateSupplierProfile({ bankDetails: ... })` which hits a different endpoint. Both update the supplier's bank information, but through completely separate API paths with different validation rules. The KYC bank flow includes IFSC lookup validation and sets bankVerificationStatus, while the Profile flow just saves raw data. A user could save bank details in Profile bypassing the KYC verification flow entirely.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.010 covers 'Two conflicting bank detail update paths between Profile and KYC pages'. This is the SAME finding — the code has not been fixed. DUPLICATE. Excluding from net-new count.
netNewFindings.impact: Supplier saves bank details in Profile tab, bypasses KYC verification entirely, but payouts may fail because bankVerificationStatus is never set to verified.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Either: (a) Remove bank details from Profile page and redirect to KYC, or (b) Make Profile bank save trigger the same verification flow as KYC.

netNewFindings.title: Onboard page stores applicationId in localStorage which persists after logout and across sessions
netNewFindings.description: The onboard page stores the applicationId in localStorage after OTP verification. Unlike sessionStorage (which clears on tab close), localStorage persists indefinitely. If a user logs out and another person uses the same browser, the applicationId from the previous session is still accessible. This could allow the second user to resume or interfere with the first user's application. The register page correctly uses sessionStorage for the same purpose.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.025 covers 'localStorage stale data persists after session expiry causing ghost auth'. That finding is about auth tokens in localStorage, not applicationId. The onboard page specifically stores business application IDs, which is a different concern. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Shared device scenario (common in Indian retail): supplier A registers on a shared browser, supplier B could see supplier A's applicationId and potentially interact with their application.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Change from localStorage to sessionStorage for applicationId storage. Add cleanup in the logout flow.

netNewFindings.title: Email verification modal is 135 lines of inline JSX in layout instead of extracted component
netNewFindings.description: The email verification modal (lines 320-438) is a 118-line inline JSX block within the dashboard layout component. It manages its own loading state, error messages, API calls for send/verify/resend, and code input. This makes the layout file 451 lines, violates single-responsibility, and makes the verification flow hard to test in isolation. The logout confirmation modal correctly uses the shared Modal component, but the verification modal does not.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.009 covers 'Email verification modal not using shared Modal component'. This finding extends beyond just the Modal component — it identifies the 118-line inline JSX as an architectural debt that makes the layout untestable. The core issue (not using Modal) is the same, but the scope (135 lines of unextracted logic) is net new detail. PARTIALLY_OVERLAPS.
netNewFindings.impact: Dashboard layout is 451 lines. The verification logic cannot be unit-tested without rendering the full layout. Any change to verification flow requires editing the layout file.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Extract into `<EmailVerificationModal isOpen={showVerificationModal} onClose={...} onVerified={refreshProfile} />` component.

netNewFindings.title: Earnings page payout detail modal fetches data but has no error state for failed fetch
netNewFindings.description: When a payout detail row is clicked, it opens a modal and fetches payout orders. The TanStack Query for payout orders uses `enabled: !!selectedPayoutId` but the modal rendering only handles the loading state (spinner) and success state (data display). There is no error state handling — if getPayoutOrders fails, the modal shows nothing after the spinner disappears (empty content in the modal body). Other pages like BNPL and orders correctly handle isError with retry buttons.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers earnings page error handling specifically. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: If the payout orders API returns a 500 or network error, user sees an empty modal with no indication of what went wrong and no retry option.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix:
Add `isError` destructuring from useQuery and render an error state with retry button inside the modal: `{isError &&
Failed to load.
}`

netNewFindings.title: Auth layout uses raw tags instead of Next.js Image component, missing optimization
netNewFindings.description: The auth layout (lines 16-17), help layout (line 17), dashboard layout (lines 122, 239-240), and register layout all use raw `` HTML tags for brand logos instead of Next.js `` component. Next.js Image provides automatic lazy loading, size optimization, WebP conversion, and prevents layout shift. For SVG logos the optimization benefit is minimal, but the pattern inconsistency and missing width/height on some usages could cause layout shifts.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers raw vs Next.js Image. R5.SUP.019 covers anchor tags vs Link, which is a similar category (HTML vs Next.js component). But Image component usage is not covered. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Minor — SVGs are already small. But using for the brand logo means no automatic format optimization and potential layout shift if width/height are omitted.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Replace `` with `import Image from 'next/image'` and `` for all brand logo usages.

netNewFindings.title: Notification timestamps use inline toLocaleString without timezone, inconsistent with formatters.ts
netNewFindings.description: The notifications page (line 152) formats timestamps inline with `new Date(n.createdAt).toLocaleString('en-IN', { day: '2-digit', month: 'short', hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' })` without specifying a timeZone. The shared formatters.ts always uses `timeZone: 'Asia/Kolkata'` (TZ constant on line 6). This means notification timestamps could show in the browser's local timezone rather than IST, while all other dates across the portal show in IST.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers timezone inconsistency in notification formatting. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: For users outside IST timezone (e.g., NRIs managing supplier accounts), notification times appear in their local timezone while all other dates show IST.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Import and use `formatDateTime` from `@/lib/formatters` instead of inline toLocaleString.

netNewFindings.title: BNPL page uses custom date formatter ignoring shared formatters.ts, inconsistent date format
netNewFindings.description: The BNPL page defines its own `fmtDate` function (lines 50-54) that formats dates as DD/MM/YYYY by splitting the ISO string. This ignores the shared `formatDate` from formatters.ts which formats as '5 Feb 2026'. The BNPL page shows dates like '24/02/2026' while every other page shows '24 Feb 2026'. Additionally, the custom fmtDate assumes ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD` and will break if the API returns a full ISO datetime string like `2026-02-24T10:00:00Z`.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers BNPL date formatting inconsistency. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Inconsistent date format across portal — BNPL shows DD/MM/YYYY while everything else shows 'D Mon YYYY'. Also fragile: if API changes date format, fmtDate breaks silently.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Replace `fmtDate(order.dueDate)` with `formatDate(order.dueDate)` from `@/lib/formatters`.

netNewFindings.title: Help & Support sidebar link navigates to /help which exits dashboard layout into standalone help layout
netNewFindings.description: The sidebar navigation (line 31) includes `{ href: '/help', label: 'Help & Support', icon: HelpCircle }`. But /help is a top-level route with its own standalone layout (help/layout.tsx) that has no sidebar, no auth guard, and a completely different visual design. Clicking 'Help & Support' in the sidebar causes a full page navigation away from the dashboard to a standalone page that looks like an unauthenticated page. The user loses their dashboard context and must navigate back manually.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers the sidebar-to-standalone help page navigation break. R5.SUP.019 covers anchor tags vs Link but not this route structure issue. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Clicking Help in the sidebar is disorienting — the entire dashboard UI disappears and is replaced by a minimal standalone page with no way back except browser back button.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Either: (a) Move help content into the (dashboard) route group as (dashboard)/help/page.tsx, or (b) Open help in a new tab/modal, or (c) Add a prominent 'Back to Dashboard' link on the help page.

netNewFindings.title: Forgot password OTP flow does not validate phone number ownership before allowing password reset
netNewFindings.description: The forgot password page has an OTP flow: user enters phone -> OTP sent -> OTP verified -> set new password. However, the phone OTP only proves the user controls the phone number — it does not verify this phone number belongs to the account being reset. If the backend does not cross-validate phone-to-account ownership during the reset-password API call, any user who knows a supplier's phone number could reset their password. The email flow has a similar but less risky concern (email link goes to the registered email). This is a backend concern but the frontend should display which account is being reset after OTP verification.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers phone-to-account validation in password reset. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: If backend does not validate phone-account binding, an attacker with access to the OTP (e.g., SIM swap) could reset any account that shares that phone number.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: After OTP verification, display the account identifier (masked email or business name) so the user confirms they are resetting the right account. Ensure backend validates phone belongs to exactly one active account.

netNewFindings.title: Body scroll lock for verification modal and sidebar uses direct DOM manipulation, may conflict with Modal component
netNewFindings.description: The dashboard layout (lines 56-61) manages body overflow via `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` for both the verification modal and sidebar. The shared Modal component (Modal.tsx lines 13-17) also manages body overflow independently. If the verification modal opens and then the user opens the logout modal (via a keyboard shortcut or edge case), both Modal.tsx and the layout will try to manage body overflow. When one closes, it may restore overflow to '' even though the other is still open.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.016 covers 'Missing scroll-to-top on page navigation and modal scroll locks'. That finding is about scroll-to-top, not about conflicting scroll lock between two independent systems. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Edge case: if verification modal and another scroll-locking element are open simultaneously, closing one unlocks scroll for both.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Use a centralized scroll lock counter pattern: increment on lock, decrement on unlock, only set overflow='' when counter reaches 0. Or use the shared Modal component for the verification modal (eliminates dual management).

netNewFindings.title: Product create/edit form lacks field-level validation feedback, only shows toast on submit
netNewFindings.description: The product creation form validates barcode format (GTIN: 8/12/13/14 digits) and price (must be positive) but only at submit time via toast.error. There is no inline field-level validation showing 'Invalid barcode format' next to the barcode field as the user types. The password reset page has a PasswordChecklist component showing real-time validation, but the product form (which has more complex validation rules) has none. For suppliers entering 50+ products, only learning about validation errors after clicking Save is slow.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: R5.SUP.007 covers price input paise conversion feedback loop. This finding is about missing field-level validation feedback across all product fields (barcode, price, name), not specifically the paise conversion. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Supplier fills out a product form, clicks Save, and only then learns the barcode is invalid. They fix it, click Save again, and learn the price is invalid. This is serial-error-discovery.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add inline validation messages under each field. Show barcode format validation on blur. Show price validation in real-time. Add a PasswordChecklist-like component for product form validation.

netNewFindings.title: Order detail panel has no keyboard-accessible close mechanism (Escape key)
netNewFindings.description: The orders page renders order details in a side panel/expanded view when an order is selected (`selectedOrder !== null`). However, there is no Escape key handler to close the detail panel. The Modal component and verification modal both handle Escape key via backdrop click, but the order detail panel is not a modal — it's an inline expansion. Other portals (retailer-admin) typically support Escape to close detail views. Additionally, there is no visible close button (X) on the order detail panel itself.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers keyboard accessibility of the order detail panel. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Keyboard-only users and users relying on assistive technology cannot close the order detail panel without tabbing to the order list and selecting a different order.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add a useEffect that listens for Escape key and calls setSelectedOrder(null). Add a visible close (X) button in the detail panel header.

netNewFindings.title: API_BASE_URL configuration allows arbitrary origin override via client-side environment variable
netNewFindings.description: The API_BASE_URL is configured from `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (line 4). Because it uses the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, this value is embedded in the client-side JavaScript bundle at build time. If an attacker can modify the build environment (supply chain attack) or if a misconfigured CI/CD sets this to a malicious URL, all API calls including auth token exchange would be sent to the attacker's server. The `credentials: 'include'` setting would also send cookies to the attacker's domain if CORS allows it.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers API_BASE_URL supply chain risk. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: If NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL is set to a malicious URL during build, all supplier authentication tokens and data are exfiltrated.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add build-time validation in next.config.js to verify API_BASE_URL is either empty string (relative) or matches an allowlist of known domains. The existing FIX-004 check only validates it is defined, not that it points to a trusted domain.

netNewFindings.title: IFSC code validation regex on profile page only validates on submit, no validation on KYC IFSC lookup field
netNewFindings.description: The profile page validates IFSC format on submit (line 137: `!/^[A-Z]{4}0[A-Z0-9]{6}$/.test(bankData.ifscCode)`). But the IFSC input field also has a pattern attribute (line 414) and auto-uppercases on change (line 409). There is a mismatch: the pattern attribute enables HTML5 form validation which shows a browser-native tooltip, while the submit handler shows a toast.error. Both fire on submit, causing potentially two validation messages. Additionally, the IFSC input accepts lowercase while the regex only matches uppercase — the toUpperCase() transform fixes this, but if a user pastes via right-click (bypassing onChange), lowercase could slip through.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers dual IFSC validation (HTML5 pattern + JS regex) or paste bypass. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: User sees both browser's native 'Please match the format' tooltip AND the toast.error for invalid IFSC. Double-error is confusing.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Remove the HTML5 pattern attribute and rely solely on the JS validation. Or add a blur handler that uppercases the value to handle paste scenarios.

netNewFindings.title: Idle timeout warning modal and logout happen client-side only, no server-side session invalidation
netNewFindings.description: The auth.tsx idle timeout (30 min with 5-min warning) calls `logout()` client-side when the timer expires. But the server-side session (HttpOnly cookies) remains valid until the cookie's own expiry. If an attacker gains access to the cookies (e.g., through a browser extension), they can continue to use the session even after the client-side idle timeout has fired. The idle timeout gives a false sense of security — it only protects against the same browser, not against cookie theft.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers the client-only nature of idle timeout. LIVE.SUP.AUTH.SERVER_SIDE_ENFORCEMENT.001 covers server-side enforcement but for limited mode, not idle timeout. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Supplier leaves their browser open, client-side timeout fires at 30 min, but the server session may be valid for hours. If cookies were somehow exfiltrated before timeout, they remain usable.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: When idle timeout fires, call a server-side session invalidation endpoint (e.g., POST /api/v1/supplier/auth/invalidate-session) in addition to clearing client-side state. Alternatively, ensure server-side cookie expiry matches the idle timeout.

netNewFindings.title: Chat page reads useSearchParams in render without Suspense boundary, will cause SSR build warning
netNewFindings.description: The chat page calls `useSearchParams()` at line 59 outside of a Suspense boundary. In Next.js App Router with static generation, this causes a build warning: 'useSearchParams() should be wrapped in a suspense boundary'. The reset-password page correctly wraps its component in Suspense (reset-password/page.tsx imports Suspense), but the chat page does not. While the chat page is 'use client' and unlikely to be statically generated, the missing Suspense boundary is a correctness issue that could cause hydration problems.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers missing Suspense for useSearchParams in chat page. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Next.js may emit a build warning. In worst case, SSR render may bail out to client-side rendering for the entire page, losing SEO and increasing time-to-interactive.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Wrap the chat page component in a Suspense boundary, or defer searchParams reading to a useEffect.

netNewFindings.title: Dashboard page has no auto-refresh or poll interval for stats, showing stale data until manual navigation
netNewFindings.description: The dashboard page uses TanStack Query with default staleTime (60s from Providers.tsx) but no refetchInterval. This means after the initial load, the stats (total products, pending orders, revenue) will remain stale until the user navigates away and back. Other pages like chat (10s), orders SSE, and the dashboard layout badge count all have refresh mechanisms. The main dashboard — which is the landing page — shows stale data.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers dashboard stats staleness. R5.SUP.014 covers first-page-only calculation accuracy. This is about temporal staleness (data not refreshing). Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Supplier receives a new order but dashboard still shows the old count until they navigate away and return. Given this is the first thing they see, stale stats give wrong impression of business activity.
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add `refetchInterval: 60000` (or 120000) to the dashboard stats query to periodically refresh.

netNewFindings.title: Pending approval page is accessible without authentication and leaks review timeline information
netNewFindings.description: The pending-approval page (71 lines) is in the (auth) route group with no auth guard. It shows static content about the review process including timeline (1-2 business days) and contact information. While this is intentional (supplier lands here after registration before approval), the page is accessible to anyone who knows the URL. It reveals internal business process details (review timeline, support email, what happens during review) to unauthenticated users.
netNewFindings.dedupeCheck: No existing finding covers pending-approval page accessibility. Net new.
netNewFindings.impact: Low — the information is not sensitive. But competitors or bad actors could learn about the review process and timeline. Also, there is no way for the user to check their actual application status from this page (no status API call).
netNewFindings.suggestedFix: Add an applicationId query parameter and fetch actual status from the API. If no applicationId, show generic content. This makes the page useful for checking status rather than just static text.
